title: Automatically select statistical tests for quantitative variables — find.test
text: level strata less five non-missing observations, statistical test performed variable, warning issued. Otherwise, appropriate test selected based following criteria: Two Groups (strata 2 levels): t-test (t.test): selected sample sizes groups \(\ge 30\) Shapiro-Wilk tests indicate normality groups. Variance equality tested using F-test. Mann-Whitney test (wilcox.test): selected sample sizes small, \(< 30\) group, normality rejected either group. Two Groups (strata > 2 levels): ANOVA (oneway.test): selected ANOVA model residuals adhere normal distribution according Shapiro-Wilk test. Homoscedasticity tested via Bartlett's test. Kruskal-Wallis test (kruskal.test): selected ANOVA residuals deviate normality.

title: Automatically select statistical tests for quantitative variables — find.test
code: df <- as.data.frame(gtsummary::trial) df$trt <- factor(df$trt) df$grade <- factor(df$grade)  # Two levels variable (trt: Drug A, Drug B) tests2 <- find.test(df, variables = c(age, marker), strata = trt) tests2  # Use outputs directly with tbl_summary() gtsummary::tbl_summary(df, include = c(age, marker), by = trt) |>   gtsummary::add_p(test = tests2$test, test.args = tests2$test.args)  # Three levels variable (grade: I, II, III) tests3 <- find.test(df, variables = c(age, marker), strata = grade) tests3  # Use outputs directly with tbl_summary() gtsummary::tbl_summary(df, include = c(age, marker), by = grade) |>   gtsummary::add_p(test = tests3$test, test.args = tests3$test.args)    # Using function show.p() from BiMaUmisc package gtsummary::tbl_summary(df, include = c(age, marker), by = grade) |>   gtsummary::add_p(test = tests3$test, test.args = tests3$test.args,                    pvalue_fun = function(x) show.p(x))

title: Format p-values for display — show.p
text: number decimals shown depends magnitude p-value two meaningful digits displayed leading zeros. Specifically: \(p \ge 0.1\), two decimal places shown. \(0.01 \le p < 0.1\), three decimal places shown. \(0.001 \le p < 0.01\), four decimal places shown. \(0.0001 \le p < 0.001\), five decimal places shown. \(p < 0.0001\), string "<0.0001" returned. formatting ensures first non-zero decimal \(p\)-value following digit displayed, avoiding excessive number leading zeros. add.p = TRUE, prefix "*p*=" ("*p*<" applicable) added formatted value. ensure p appears cursive calling function line R markdown documents.

title: Plot survival curves — survival.plot
code: # CAUTION: Before running through the Console, read Note to ensure proper  # visualization (how to modify dimensions of the Plot window). lung <- survival::cancer lung$time_y <- lung$time/365.25 lung$sex <- factor(lung$sex, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Male", "Female"))  # no strata survival.plot(lung, time_y, status, units = "y") # customizing survival.plot(lung, time_y, status, units = "y",               xlab = "Time since diagnosis (in years)",               yscale = 100,               main = "Overall survival", mark.col = "darkgray")  # 2 strata survival.plot(lung, time_y, status, sex, units = "y") # customizing survival.plot(lung, time_y, status, sex,                legend.pos = "topright", legend.title = "Sex",                events = TRUE, risk.text = FALSE, p.value.pos = c(2.4, 0.4),               units = "y", xlab = "Time since diagnosis (in years)",                main = "Overall survival", col = c("darkviolet", "darkgreen"))
